title: As It Is Played
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 188
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM, no library): two walls of eight online chess games replaying on small boards, one drawn by chance in the visitor's browser from sixty games people played, one chosen from the same sixty by a machine selector asked for the games 'as it is'; the visitor guesses which wall is chance, then the sixty open with the dots of the eighteen selectors who chose each game and their reasons, any game replayable, and a table against 100,000 random eights; two guesses handed to the house's study frame. A figure (figure.svg). Python for the frame, the draw, scoring and the face's data; every version of every selector's eight, their notes and after-answers in selections/.
embodies: Asked for eight games that show how people play chess online 'as it is', six machine selectors with sixty real games in hand did not pick the showpieces: they counted the sixty and built a copy of it at small scale (checkmates 27.1 % of picks, the sixty 26.7 %). Every one of their eights, and every eight of six selectors given the counts, sits closer to the sixty's mix of endings than five random eights in six do, and only one of the twelve holds a draw where a random eight holds one 35.5 % of the time. Asked for the eight most worth showing, six more chose the specimen (50 % checkmates). Chance is lumpier than the machine's picture of it.
result: P1 failed (A checkmates 27.1 %, falsifier at or below 31.7). P2 failed (A on time 35.4 %, falsifier 27 or more). P3 failed (A over before move 15: 6 of 48, falsifier 5 or more). P4 neither (A 22.9 points below C; bounds 15 and 25). P5 held (6 of 6 B eights within 2.0 games of the endings; all at 1.2). P6 failed (B over before move 15: 7 of 48). P7 held (A median pairwise overlap 2; random 1.07). P8 held (all 18 estimate 8 short games of 60, the true count, and 16 or 18 checkmates). Post hoc: all 12 A and B eights within 1.73 games of the sixty's ending mix (random eights 16.4 %); eights with a draw A 0, B 1, C 6 of 6 (random 35.5 %); C median overlap 5; 4 of 6 A selectors counted the sixty in their first version.
project_step: Sixty-second experiment. Operations: choosing material (main: choosing within found material), judging, perceiving, iterating, varying, erring. Takes from experiments 57 and 61 the finding that only material the maker did not arrange, or numbers where they count, move the maker's type; and from 61 its arm G (the people's numbers told), moved here from making to selecting (arm B). Asks whether selection from the people's own material, the method a researcher reaches for after making fails, brings the type back. Works against Cartography, not Tracing in the making: the face sets a tracing (the selectors' scale copy) beside a map (a chance draw) for the visitor to tell apart.
material: Online chess as people play it: the Lichess open database, standard rated games of October 2026 (CC0); 128,323 complete games in the first 40 MiB of the month's file (1 October 2026, 00:00:25 to 01:46:39 UTC); 400 drawn by seed 188, the first 60 the selectors' pool. Domain: games and play (chess).

data_sources.what: Lichess open database, standard rated games, October 2026, CC0; first 40 MiB read by range request on 2026-11-26; frame of 128,323 complete games; player names, links and clocks dropped; features computed by replaying the moves (python-chess 1.11.2)
Lichess open database index: licence (CC0) and monthly files
Chess.com, how games end by time control (19.8 million games in 24 hours, 2025): read in the field search, not used as a figure

Eicher and Irgolič, 'Compensatory Biases Under Cognitive Load: Reducing Selection Bias in Large Language Models' (arXiv:2402.01740): list-selection bias as primacy; the field search found no test of a model choosing a representative subset of found material against the archive's distribution

rights: Games are CC0 (Lichess open database); player names and links are removed. Selectors' versions, notes, derived counts and code CC BY 4.0 / Apache 2.0 (house line).
seed: 188 (draw of 400 from the frame, order); 1880, 1881, 1882 (random eights for the null, the closeness count and the figure); the face's chance wall is drawn fresh in each visitor's browser; selectors are model instances and not seeded
